s:
Which of the following grounds are expressly mentioned in Article 15(1) as prohibited grounds of discrimination?
1. Religion
2. Race
3. Caste
4. Sex
5. Place of birth
6. Descent
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Article 15(1) prohibits discrimination only on the grounds of religion, race, caste, sex and place of birth. Descent is specifically added in Article 16(2), not Article 15(1).
tq: Separate the closely related grounds in Articles 15 and 16 instead of treating their lists as identical.
sec: Articles 14-18 - content and clause text  [APPSC]

s:
Article 15(2) prohibits denial of access, on the specified grounds of discrimination, to which of the following?
1. Shops and public restaurants
2. Hotels
3. Wells, tanks and bathing ghats
4. Places of public entertainment
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The listed places under Article 15(2) are shops, restaurants, hotels, wells, tanks and bathing ghats. Places of public entertainment are not included in the specified list given here.
tq: Test the exact statutory list and reject an attractive but unlisted addition.
sec: Articles 14-18 - content and clause text  [APPSC]

s: A private hotel refuses entry to a person solely on the ground of caste. Which constitutional provision is most directly attracted?
x: Article 15(2) applies to access to places such as hotels and binds private persons as well as the State. It prohibits discrimination on the specified grounds in such access.
tq: Apply the clause to a private-person situation rather than assuming that equality provisions bind only the State.
sec: Articles 14-18 - content and clause text  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Articles 14 and 15?
o: Article 14 applies to all persons, whereas Article 15 is available only to citizens.
Article 14 applies only to citizens, whereas Article 15 applies to all persons.
Both Articles 14 and 15 are available only to citizens.
Both Articles 14 and 15 apply only to foreigners residing in India.
x: Article 14 applies to any person within the territory of India. Article 15 is a right available only to citizens.
tq: Discriminate between the beneficiaries of two neighbouring constitutional provisions.
sec: Articles 14-18 - content and clause text  [APPSC]

s:
With reference to Article 16, consider the following statements:
1. It guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.
2. Descent and residence are among the grounds added to the prohibited list under Article 16(2).
3. Parliament alone may prescribe residence requirements for certain public employment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Article 16 concerns equality of opportunity in public employment. Article 16(2) includes descent and residence, while Article 16(3) permits Parliament to prescribe residence requirements for certain jobs.
tq: Combine the general guarantee with the specific clauses and the authority competent to act.
sec: Articles 14-18 - content and clause text  [APPSC]

s: Under Article 16(3), which body is competent to prescribe a residence requirement for certain public employment?
o: The Governor of the concerned State
x: Article 16(3) specifically empowers Parliament to prescribe residence requirements for certain classes of employment or appointment under a State or Union territory.
tq: Use the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the constitutionally specified authority.
sec: Articles 14-18 - content and clause text  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following statements regarding Article 17 is correct?
o: It abolishes titles conferred by the State.
It abolishes untouchability and makes the enforcement of any disability arising from it an offence.
It prohibits discrimination only on grounds of religion and race.
It abolishes untouchability only in government offices.
x: Article 17 abolishes untouchability, forbids its practice and treats enforcement of any disability arising from it as an offence.
tq: Match the constitutional article with both its prohibition and its legal consequence.
sec: Articles 14-18 - content and clause text  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Article 18 — Equality of opportunity in public employment
x: Article 17 deals with the abolition of untouchability. Article 14 concerns equality before law, Article 15 discrimination, and Article 18 titles.
tq: Use article-subject matching and eliminate provisions assigned to neighbouring articles.
sec: Articles 14-18 - content and clause text  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Articles 39(b), 39(c) and 39(d), which are Directive Principles, are associated with economic equality. Social equality is associated with Articles 15, 17 and 18.
tq: Identify the reversed comparison in a classification table.
sec: Types of equality - article securing each  [APPSC]

s: The constitutional provisions relating to no exclusion from electoral rolls on specified grounds and adult suffrage primarily secure which type of equality?
x: Articles 325 and 326 are associated with political equality through non-exclusion from electoral rolls and adult suffrage.
tq: Connect a constitutional mechanism with the type of equality it advances.
sec: Types of equality - article securing each  [APPSC]

s: According to B. R. Ambedkar, liberty, equality and fraternity are best understood as:
o: Economic objectives confined to the Directive Principles
Three independent ideals applicable to separate institutions
Duties imposed only on public servants
x: Ambedkar described liberty, equality and fraternity as an inseparable trinity.
tq: Recall the precise formulation associated with the constitutional thinker.
sec: Types of equality - article securing each  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following special provisions is correctly matched with its beneficiary group?
o: Article 16(4) — Foreign citizens inadequately represented in services
Article 16(5) — All religious minorities in public employment
x: Article 15(3), part of the original Constitution, permits special provisions for women and children. The other pairings misstate the beneficiary groups or scope of the relevant clauses.
tq: Start from the sure beneficiary-clause pair and reject swapped groups.
sec: Articles 15 and 16 special provisions - beneficiaries, groups not covered  [APPSC]

s: Article 15(4), inserted by the First Constitutional Amendment, 1951, provides for special provisions for:
o: Socially and educationally backward classes, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
x: Article 15(4) covers socially and educationally backward classes, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. It was inserted by the First Amendment in 1951.
tq: Link an amendment number and year with the precise beneficiary group.
sec: Articles 15 and 16 special provisions - beneficiaries, groups not covered  [APPSC]

s: Which statement regarding Article 15(5) is correct?
o: It applies to public employment and excludes all educational institutions.
It applies only to government educational institutions.
It permits special provisions for SEBCs, SCs and STs in admissions to private aided or unaided institutions, except minority institutions.
It covers only women and children in private institutions.
x: Article 15(5), inserted by the 93rd Amendment, 2005, covers admissions in private aided or unaided educational institutions for SEBCs, SCs and STs, but excludes minority institutions under Article 30.
tq: Use the scope trap involving private institutions and the minority-institution exception.
sec: Articles 15 and 16 special provisions - beneficiaries, groups not covered  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following groups is NOT covered by the special provisions specifically described under Article 15?
x: The listed Article 15 special provisions cover women, children, SEBCs, SCs, STs and, under Article 15(6), EWS. Aged persons are not included in this list.
tq: Find the excluded group rather than selecting a group expressly named in the provision.
sec: Articles 15 and 16 special provisions - beneficiaries, groups not covered  [APPSC]

s: The reservation contemplated by Article 16(4) relates to backward classes which:
o: Are identified solely on the basis of age
Are represented only in private employment
Are not adequately represented in the services under the State
x: Article 16(4) permits reservation for backward classes that, in the opinion of the State, are not adequately represented in the services under it.
tq: Read the qualifying condition carefully: the constitutional test is inadequate representation in services.
sec: Articles 15 and 16 special provisions - beneficiaries, groups not covered  [APPSC]

s: Which provision permits reservation in promotion for members of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
x: Article 16(4A) concerns reservation in promotion for SCs and STs, along with consequential seniority as reflected in the relevant amendments.
tq: Distinguish the promotion clause from the clauses dealing with admissions, religion or foreign titles.
sec: Articles 15 and 16 special provisions - beneficiaries, groups not covered  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 77th Amendment inserted Article 16(4A).
2. The 81st Amendment dealt with carry-forward of unfilled reserved vacancies.
3. The 85th Amendment is associated with consequential seniority in promotion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The 77th Amendment, 1995, inserted Article 16(4A); the 81st Amendment, 2000, addressed carry-forward vacancies; and the 85th Amendment, 2001, provided promotion with consequential seniority.
tq: Build the answer by mapping each amendment to its distinct reservation effect.
sec: Articles 15 and 16 special provisions - beneficiaries, groups not covered  [APPSC]

s: Article 16(4B), inserted by the 81st Constitutional Amendment, deals with:
o: Reservation for women in educational institutions
Reservation for EWS up to 10 per cent
Carry-forward of unfilled reserved vacancies as a separate class outside the 50 per cent ceiling
x: Article 16(4B) treats carried-forward unfilled reserved vacancies as a separate class and places them outside the 50 per cent ceiling referred to in the provision.
tq: Use the amendment-effect pairing and retain the specific ceiling-related detail.
sec: Articles 15 and 16 special provisions - beneficiaries, groups not covered  [APPSC]

s: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment, 2019, inserted Articles 15(6) and 16(6) relating to:
o: Reservation for SCs and STs in promotions only
Reservation for EWS up to 10 per cent
x: The 103rd Amendment inserted Articles 15(6) and 16(6), providing for reservation for Economically Weaker Sections up to 10 per cent. It was passed as the 124th Amendment Bill in the Lok Sabha.
tq: Match the amendment year and clause numbers with the percentage and beneficiary group.
sec: Articles 15 and 16 special provisions - beneficiaries, groups not covered  [APPSC]

s:
Arrange the following amendments in chronological order:
A. 103rd Constitutional Amendment
B. 77th Constitutional Amendment
C. 93rd Constitutional Amendment
D. 81st Constitutional Amendment
x: The amendments were enacted in the order 77th (1995), 81st (2000), 93rd (2005) and 103rd (2019).
tq: Anchor the earliest and latest amendments first, then place the intermediate years.
sec: Articles 15 and 16 special provisions - beneficiaries, groups not covered  [APPSC]

s: Article 16(5) permits a qualification relating to religion or denomination in respect of an office connected with:
o: Every public employment under a State
x: Article 16(5) permits offices connected with religious or denominational institutions to be kept for persons professing that particular religion or belonging to that denomination.
tq: Identify the institutional exception rather than applying the religious qualification to all public employment.
sec: Articles 15 and 16 special provisions - beneficiaries, groups not covered  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following statements about Article 18(1) is correct?
o: The State may confer any hereditary title with the President’s consent.
The State shall confer no title except military or academic distinctions.
Only foreign titles are prohibited under Article 18(1).
National awards are expressly declared to be titles under Article 18(1).
x: Article 18(1) prohibits the State from conferring titles, except military and academic distinctions. The provision does not prohibit those two categories.
tq: Use the stated exception to avoid the extreme claim that every distinction is prohibited.
sec: Article 18 - titles abolished, foreign titles, consent, national awards  [APPSC]

s: Under Article 18(2), a citizen of India:
o: May accept a foreign title with the consent of the Governor
May accept only an academic title from a foreign State
Shall not accept any title from a foreign State
May accept a foreign title without restriction
x: Article 18(2) provides that no citizen of India shall accept any title from a foreign State.
tq: Distinguish the absolute constitutional bar on citizens from the consent-based rule for certain non-citizens.
sec: Article 18 - titles abolished, foreign titles, consent, national awards

s: A non-citizen holding an office of profit or trust under the State seeks to accept a title from a foreign State. Whose consent is constitutionally required?
x: Under Article 18(3), a non-citizen holding an office of profit or trust under the State requires the President’s consent to accept a foreign title.
tq: Apply the authority trap by identifying the office-holder whose consent is expressly named.
sec: Article 18 - titles abolished, foreign titles, consent, national awards

s:
No person holding an office of profit or trust under the State may accept, without the President’s consent, which of the following from a foreign State?
1. Any present
2. Any emolument
3. Any office
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Article 18(4) requires the President’s consent for a person holding an office of profit or trust under the State to accept any present, emolument or office from a foreign State.
tq: Test the complete three-part list and avoid dropping the final item.
sec: Article 18 - titles abolished, foreign titles, consent, national awards

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the effect of the decision in Balaji Raghavan v. Union of India (1996)?
o: The decision authorised award-holders to use the awards as hereditary titles.
Bharat Ratna and Padma awards were held not to be titles under Article 18, but they must not be used as prefixes or suffixes.
All national awards were held to be military distinctions only.
Bharat Ratna and Padma awards were held to be titles and were abolished.
x: The Supreme Court held that Bharat Ratna and Padma awards are not titles under Article 18. However, they cannot be used as prefixes or suffixes to a person’s name.
tq: Separate the legal status of an award from the prohibited manner of using it.
sec: Article 18 - titles abolished, foreign titles, consent, national awards

s: Bharat Ratna and Padma awards were stopped in 1977 and revived in:
x: The Bharat Ratna and Padma awards were discontinued in 1977 and revived in 1980.
tq: Use the two-event timeline and select the later revival year rather than the interruption year.
sec: Article 18 - titles abolished, foreign titles, consent, national awards

s:
Assertion (A): Article 18 is associated with social equality.
Reason (R): It seeks to end artificial distinctions created through State-conferred titles.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both statements are true. Article 18 advances social equality by abolishing artificial distinctions arising from State-conferred titles, subject to the stated exceptions.
tq: Check whether the reason directly explains why the provision advances the stated type of equality.
sec: Article 18 - titles abolished, foreign titles, consent, national awards

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes equality before law from equal protection of laws?
o: Equality before law is a positive concept of classification, whereas equal protection is a negative concept of uniformity
Equality before law is a negative concept denying special privilege, whereas equal protection is a positive concept permitting reasonable classification
Equality before law applies only to citizens, whereas equal protection applies only to foreigners
Both are negative concepts derived exclusively from the Indian Constitution
x: Equality before law is a negative concept associated with absence of special privilege and subjection of all persons to ordinary law. Equal protection of laws is a positive concept requiring like treatment in like circumstances and permitting reasonable classification.
tq: Split the options by comparing the origin, character and legal effect of the two expressions.
sec: Article 14 - equality before law vs equal protection, rule of law, arbitrariness, classification  [APPSC]

s: The expression ‘equality before law’ is primarily associated with which of the following?
o: The British doctrine of Dicey's rule of law
The Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms
The French Declaration of the Rights of Man
The American doctrine under the Fourteenth Amendment
x: Equality before law has British origins and is associated with Dicey's rule of law. Equal protection of laws is associated with the American Fourteenth Amendment.
tq: Use the origin-based distinction to separate two constitutionally similar expressions.
sec: Article 14 - equality before law vs equal protection, rule of law, arbitrariness, classification  [APPSC]

s:
With reference to the rule of law as explained by A.V. Dicey, consider the following statements:
1. It involves the absence of arbitrary power.
2. It requires equality before law.
3. It means that rights flow from the Constitution rather than being declared by courts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Dicey's elements include absence of arbitrary power, equality before law and the predominance of legal spirit. India accepts the first two elements, but in India rights flow from the Constitution rather than being the result of rights declared by courts.
tq: Find the statement that reverses the Indian position on the source of rights.
sec: Article 14 - equality before law vs equal protection, rule of law, arbitrariness, classification  [APPSC]

s: The rule of law is regarded as which of the following in the Indian constitutional system?
o: A power available only to the executive
A directive applicable only during an Emergency
A basic feature of the Constitution
x: The rule of law is recognised as a basic feature of the Constitution and cannot be destroyed by constitutional amendment.
tq: Identify the constitutional status of the doctrine rather than its individual components.
sec: Article 14 - equality before law vs equal protection, rule of law, arbitrariness, classification  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following are recognised exceptions to the ordinary operation of equality before law?
1. Immunity of the President and Governors from criminal proceedings during their term of office
2. Special position of foreign diplomats
3. Immunities of United Nations agencies
4. Immunity of every public servant from civil proceedings
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The recognised exceptions include constitutional immunity of the President and Governors during their term, diplomatic immunity and immunities of UN agencies. There is no general immunity for every public servant from civil proceedings.
tq: Eliminate the overbroad statement extending an exception to every public servant.
sec: Article 14 - equality before law vs equal protection, rule of law, arbitrariness, classification  [APPSC]

s: Under Article 361, a civil proceeding against the President or a Governor during the term of office can be instituted only after—
x: Article 361 protects the President and Governors from civil proceedings during their term unless the prescribed two months' notice has been given.
tq: Focus on the precise notice period instead of the broader immunity principle.
sec: Article 14 - equality before law vs equal protection, rule of law, arbitrariness, classification  [APPSC]

s: In which case did the Supreme Court state that ‘equality is antithetic to arbitrariness’ or that equality and arbitrariness are sworn enemies?
o: M.R. Balaji v. State of Mysore
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
E.P. Royappa v. State of Tamil Nadu
x: E.P. Royappa v. State of Tamil Nadu (1974) established the close constitutional relationship between equality and non-arbitrariness.
tq: Match the distinctive judicial formulation with the case in which it was stated.
sec: Article 14 - equality before law vs equal protection, rule of law, arbitrariness, classification  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following propositions is associated with Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978) in the context of Article 14?
o: Class legislation is always valid if enacted by Parliament
Any arbitrary State action violates Article 14
Article 14 applies only to taxation laws
x: Maneka Gandhi reinforced the principle that arbitrary State action is inconsistent with Article 14. Unguided discretionary power may therefore be struck down.
tq: Use the case-law principle rather than confusing it with the classification test.
sec: Article 14 - equality before law vs equal protection, rule of law, arbitrariness, classification  [APPSC]

s: A law creates two groups for different treatment. For the classification to be valid under Article 14, which combination is required?
o: Intelligible differentia and rational nexus with the object of the law
x: The twin test of reasonable classification is an intelligible differentia distinguishing the grouped persons or things and a rational nexus between the differentia and the object sought to be achieved.
tq: Apply the twin test to distinguish reasonable classification from class legislation.
sec: Article 14 - equality before law vs equal protection, rule of law, arbitrariness, classification  [APPSC]

s: Article 14 forbids—
o: class legislation, while permitting reasonable classification
reasonable classification based on intelligible differentia
x: Article 14 does not prohibit classification as such. It prohibits class legislation and permits classification satisfying intelligible differentia and rational nexus.
tq: Watch for the extreme word ‘all’ and distinguish class legislation from reasonable classification.
sec: Article 14 - equality before law vs equal protection, rule of law, arbitrariness, classification  [APPSC]

s: The Supreme Court’s April 2026 ruling concerning pensioners and serving employees reaffirmed that the State—
o: must abolish dearness allowance for pensioners
cannot treat pensioners differently from serving employees on dearness allowance without constitutionally valid justification
may always treat pensioners differently from serving employees on dearness allowance
can classify employees only on the basis of residence
x: The ruling held that the State cannot arbitrarily treat pensioners differently from serving employees in relation to dearness allowance. The classification must satisfy Article 14 requirements.
tq: Apply non-arbitrariness and rational classification to a concrete administrative distinction.
sec: Article 14 - equality before law vs equal protection, rule of law, arbitrariness, classification  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 17:
1. Untouchability is expressly defined in the Constitution.
2. Article 17 operates against private persons also.
3. Article 17 belongs to the Right to Equality group.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Constitution does not define ‘untouchability’. Article 17 is a Fundamental Right within the Right to Equality group and can operate against private persons as well.
tq: Reject the precise-sounding but false claim that the Constitution defines untouchability.
sec: Article 17 - untouchability, category, enforcing laws  [other exams]

s: Which one of the following Acts specifically addresses atrocities against members of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
o: SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
National Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993
x: The SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 addresses atrocities against members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 primarily concerns enforcement against untouchability.
tq: Discriminate between two related laws by matching each law with its specific subject.
sec: Article 17 - untouchability, category, enforcing laws  [other exams]

s: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 are overseen by which department?
x: Both Acts are overseen by the Department of Social Justice.
tq: Use the responsible administrative department as the identifying fact.
sec: Article 17 - untouchability, category, enforcing laws  [other exams]

s: Who is associated with ensuring that Article 17 made untouchability a punishable offence?
x: B.R. Ambedkar ensured that Article 17 constitutionally treated untouchability as a punishable offence.
tq: Match the constitutional contribution with the principal figure associated with it.
sec: Article 17 - untouchability, category, enforcing laws  [other exams]

s:
Arrange the following cases in chronological order:
A. M.R. Balaji
B. Champakam Dorairajan
C. Indra Sawhney
D. M. Nagaraj
x: The cases were decided in the order Champakam Dorairajan (1951), M.R. Balaji (1963), Indra Sawhney (1992) and M. Nagaraj (2006).
tq: Fix the earliest and latest cases first, then place the two intermediate rulings.
sec: Reservation cases - ruling issue, creamy layer and 50% ceiling origin

s: The Supreme Court struck down the Communal Government Order in Champakam Dorairajan primarily under—
x: In Champakam Dorairajan (1951), the Communal G.O. was struck down under Article 29(2). The case also established the then-prevailing position that Directive Principles were subordinate to Fundamental Rights, leading to the First Amendment and Article 15(4).
tq: Match the case with the specific constitutional provision involved in its ruling.
sec: Reservation cases - ruling issue, creamy layer and 50% ceiling origin

s: Which case is associated with the proposition that reservation should generally remain below 50 per cent?
x: M.R. Balaji (1963) stated that reservation should generally remain below 50 per cent.
tq: Associate the numerical ceiling principle with the case that first articulated it.
sec: Reservation cases - ruling issue, creamy layer and 50% ceiling origin

s:
With reference to Indra Sawhney (1992), consider the following statements:
1. It upheld 27 per cent reservation for Other Backward Classes.
2. It introduced the exclusion of the creamy layer.
3. It upheld reservation in promotions as a general rule.
4. It recognised a 50 per cent ceiling, subject to extraordinary situations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Indra Sawhney upheld the 27 per cent OBC quota, introduced the creamy-layer exclusion and recognised the 50 per cent ceiling subject to extraordinary situations. It did not uphold reservation in promotions as a general rule.
tq: Identify the single reversed proposition concerning reservation in promotions.
sec: Reservation cases - ruling issue, creamy layer and 50% ceiling origin

s: The constitutional principle of excluding the creamy layer from reservation for Other Backward Classes originated in—
x: The creamy-layer principle originated in Indra Sawhney (1992).
tq: Distinguish the origin of a doctrine from later cases dealing with its application.
sec: Reservation cases - ruling issue, creamy layer and 50% ceiling origin

s: Which one of the following is the income limit for the OBC creamy layer mentioned in the 2017 notification?
x: The OBC creamy-layer income limit mentioned in the 2017 notification is ₹8 lakh a year. Andhra Pradesh aligned its definitions with the central thresholds.
tq: Read the figure precisely and distinguish it from nearby income thresholds.
sec: Reservation cases - ruling issue, creamy layer and 50% ceiling origin

s: Which of the following correctly describes the ruling in M. Nagaraj (2006)?
o: It introduced the 27 per cent OBC quota
It permitted sub-classification among Scheduled Castes
It upheld the 77th, 81st and 85th Amendments and required quantifiable data regarding backwardness, inadequate representation and efficiency
It struck down all amendments relating to reservation in promotions
x: M. Nagaraj upheld the 77th, 81st and 85th Amendments and required the State to show quantifiable data concerning backwardness, inadequacy of representation and administrative efficiency under Article 335.
tq: Use the case’s distinctive combination of upheld amendments and evidentiary requirements.
sec: Reservation cases - ruling issue, creamy layer and 50% ceiling origin

s: Which one of the following statements about Jarnail Singh (2018) is correct?
o: It required fresh data proving the backwardness of SCs and STs in every case
It upheld the EWS reservation under the 103rd Amendment
It abolished the creamy-layer principle for OBCs
It held that no data on SC/ST backwardness was needed and applied the creamy-layer principle to SC/ST promotions
x: Jarnail Singh (2018) held that separate data establishing backwardness of SCs and STs was not necessary, while applying the creamy-layer principle to SC/ST promotions.
tq: Separate the backwardness-data requirement from the creamy-layer requirement in promotions.
sec: Reservation cases - ruling issue, creamy layer and 50% ceiling origin

s: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment providing reservation for Economically Weaker Sections was upheld by the Supreme Court in—
x: In Janhit Abhiyan (2022), the Supreme Court upheld the 103rd Amendment providing 10 per cent EWS reservation by a 3:2 majority.
tq: Combine the case name, amendment, percentage and majority to identify the precise ruling.
sec: Reservation cases - ruling issue, creamy layer and 50% ceiling origin

s: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024) is associated with which proposition?
o: The 50 per cent ceiling is completely abolished
The creamy layer applies only to economically weaker sections
Reservation in promotions is unconstitutional in every circumstance
Sub-classification of Scheduled Castes is permitted
x: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024) permitted sub-classification of Scheduled Castes.
tq: Match the recent case with its specific reservation jurisprudence issue.
sec: Reservation cases - ruling issue, creamy layer and 50% ceiling origin

s:
Which of the following are recognised exceptions or qualifications to the 50 per cent reservation ceiling?
1. Extraordinary situations such as remote areas
2. Carry-forward of backlog vacancies under the 81st Amendment
3. EWS reservation upheld in Janhit Abhiyan
4. Every reservation made by a State legislature without limitation
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Extraordinary situations, carry-forward vacancies under the 81st Amendment and the EWS reservation recognised in Janhit Abhiyan are stated qualifications or exceptions. There is no unrestricted power for every State legislature to exceed the ceiling.
tq: Reject the absolute statement that removes all constitutional limits on reservation.
sec: Reservation cases - ruling issue, creamy layer and 50% ceiling origin

s: The National Commission for Backward Classes has constitutional status under—
x: The National Commission for Backward Classes is a constitutional body under Article 338B.
tq: Distinguish closely numbered constitutional provisions relating to commissions.
sec: Reservation cases - ruling issue, creamy layer and 50% ceiling origin

s: Which amendment-clause pair is correctly matched?
x: The First Amendment, 1951 inserted Article 15(4). Article 16(4A) was inserted by the 77th Amendment, Article 16(4B) by the 81st, Article 15(5) by the 93rd and Article 16(6) by the 103rd Amendment.
tq: Start with the sure amendment-clause pair and eliminate the swapped clauses.
sec: Amendments changing Articles 15-16 (1st, 77th, 81st, 85th, 93rd, 103rd)

s: The provision concerning carry-forward of backlog vacancies was introduced through—
o: Article 15(4), inserted by the First Amendment
x: The 81st Amendment, 2000 inserted Article 16(4B), dealing with carry-forward of unfilled reservation vacancies or backlog vacancies.
tq: Distinguish the two adjacent promotion provisions, 16(4A) and 16(4B).
sec: Amendments changing Articles 15-16 (1st, 77th, 81st, 85th, 93rd, 103rd)

s: The concept of consequential seniority in relation to Article 16(4A) was introduced by the—
x: The 85th Amendment, 2001 introduced consequential seniority in Article 16(4A), with retrospective effect from 1995.
tq: Separate the year of the amendment from its retrospective effective date.
sec: Amendments changing Articles 15-16 (1st, 77th, 81st, 85th, 93rd, 103rd)

s: Article 15(5), concerning reservation in admissions to educational institutions, was inserted by the—
x: The 93rd Amendment, 2005 inserted Article 15(5), enabling reservation in admissions to educational institutions.
tq: Match the admissions provision with the amendment that inserted it.
sec: Amendments changing Articles 15-16 (1st, 77th, 81st, 85th, 93rd, 103rd)

s: The First Constitutional Amendment inserted Article 15(4) primarily to overcome the effect of which judgment?
o: E.P. Royappa v. State of Tamil Nadu
x: Article 15(4) was inserted by the First Amendment, 1951 in response to the ruling in Champakam Dorairajan, which had struck down the Communal G.O. under Article 29(2).
tq: Link a constitutional amendment to the judgment whose effect it was intended to overcome.
sec: Amendments changing Articles 15-16 (1st, 77th, 81st, 85th, 93rd, 103rd)

s: In April 2026, the Supreme Court applied the twin test under Article 14 while considering differential treatment in dearness allowance. The case concerned which category of persons?
o: Women and men in Panchayati Raj Institutions
x: The Supreme Court held that the State cannot treat pensioners differently from serving employees in the matter of dearness allowance without satisfying Article 14's twin test.
tq: Identify the persons directly connected with the constitutional principle and the judicial ruling.
sec: Universal angles

s: The Supreme Court questioned the caste-discrimination clause of the UGC equity regulations in which case?
o: Pensioners Association v. Union of India
Mritunjay Tiwari v. State of Andhra Pradesh
